reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports improved CO oxidation activity and long-term stability with increased configurational disorder in spinel oxides, but it does not address the formation of such a surface on an alloy catalyst, nor does it provide any evidence for resistance to H2O/NO poisoning or durability under automotive aging conditions, leaving three key premises unsupported.
premises: Increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides improves CO oxidation activity (lower T10).
Increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides improves long-term stability (resistance to deactivation).
The proposed high-entropy spinel oxide surface can be formed on a multi-principal-element alloy catalyst.
The benefits of configurational disorder in spinel oxides will translate to resistance against H2O and NO poisoning.
The benefits of configurational disorder in spinel oxides will translate to durability under automotive aging conditions.
